- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 1–2% below true peak.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days of history show strong downward trend, model often underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- If sentiment is flat (0.0) and model forecast is consistently below true, consider slight upward bias correction (e.g., +0.5–1.0% for next 3–5 days).
- When model forecast is significantly higher than true outcome (e.g., >5% over 3–5 days), reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence with true trend.
- If sentiment history shows no recent positive sentiment but model forecast is rising, assume mean reversion; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.
